# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Deaf and can see the bomb but cannot hear or touch it. I will establish the required four-symbol code before any operational exchange: YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE. The gestures are sent visibly to Mute, while the spoken names reach Mute and Blind. I will use the same code consistently and expand it only if needed.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: YES is 👍, NO is 👎, HOLD is ✋, DONE is 👌. Everyone wait for the next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I see a green light, display 0, and five wires in order: red, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute’s 👍 confirms receipt of the YES code. I am sending the complete visible state to Blind and asking Mute to use the established gesture code for the manual’s verdict; if more detail is needed, I will define additional gestures.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in positions 1 through 5 are red, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute is consulting the manual; I will relay its verdict.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please consult the manual for this bomb state and gesture YES when ready, NO if it cannot determine the action, or HOLD if more code is needed.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s 👍 confirms the manual can determine the action, but it does not yet identify which wire. I am expanding the code only for that needed message: 🤛 means CUT, ✋ means HOLD, and the next gesture identifies the wire—☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, 🤚=5. Mute should send the action gesture followed by the wire number; I will decode it and tell Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual action as two gestures: 🤛 means CUT or ✋ means HOLD, followed by the wire number: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖐 is 4, and 🤚 is 5. If the manual requires a different operation, signal 👌 DONE and I will ask for more code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s ✋ means HOLD. The manual does not currently authorize cutting a wire, so Blind must not touch or alter the bomb. I am relaying the hold instruction directly.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict: HOLD. Do not cut or alter anything; wait.")
wait()
```

(empty)

No new information has arrived. The bomb remains at display 0 with green light and the same five wires, and the last manual verdict was HOLD. I will avoid inventing an action and keep Blind from changing anything.

```text
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s 👎 is the established NO signal. I cannot infer a wire or safe operation from NO alone, so Blind must continue making no changes. I will ask Mute to provide a complete, coded verdict if the manual specifies one.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute’s manual signal is NO. No wire or operation is authorized; do not touch or alter the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the complete manual verdict using the established code. If it is HOLD, signal ✋; if it is CUT, signal 🤛 followed by the wire number. Do not signal NO alone unless no action is safe.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[white] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute has again sent NO, but the preceding request bundled several possibilities, so this does not identify a safe operation or wire. I will ask one precise question: whether the manual requires cutting. Until that is answered, Blind must continue to hold.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="One precise question: does the manual require CUT? Signal YES with 👍 or NO with 👎.")
speak(to="blind", text="No complete action instruction has been received. Continue HOLD; do not touch the bomb.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s 👍 answers YES: the manual requires cutting a wire. The wire number is still unknown, so Blind must not act yet. I will request only the wire number using the code already established.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Signal the required wire number only: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖐 is 4, and 🤚 is 5.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual requires CUT, but the wire number is not known yet. Do not act until I provide it.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute’s ✋ is the established HOLD signal, not a wire number. Therefore I still have no safe wire identification, and Blind must not cut anything. I will ask Mute to send exactly one wire-number gesture when the manual identifies it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: Mute signaled HOLD, so no wire number is available. Do not cut or alter the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal exactly one wire number when known: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖐 is 4, and 🤚 is 5. Signal ✋ only if the manual says HOLD.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s 👎 is NO, so the requested wire number has not been supplied. No safe cutting instruction can be completed from the information available. Blind must continue to hold; I will ask Mute to send the wire number when the manual provides one.

```text

speak(to="mute", text="NO received. If cutting is required, signal the required wire number only: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🖐 is 4, 🤚 is 5. If no cut is required, signal HOLD with ✋.")
```
